1	# P3: Uniform correlation estimate for squarefree numbers
     2	
     3	For real x≥2 and every integer 1≤m≤x, define C_x(m)=Σ_{1≤n≤x−m}μ²(n)μ²(n+m) and 𝔖(m)=∏_p(1−2/p²)∏_{p²|m}(p²−1)/(p²−2), with products over primes. For every ε>0 there is C(ε)>0 such that |C_x(m)−(x−m)𝔖(m)|≤C(ε)x^(4/5+ε), uniformly for all such x and m. A permitted circle-method cutoff is Q=x^(2/5), for x sufficiently large that Q≤x^(1/2)/2; the major arcs are the subsets of R/Z with |α−a/q|≤Q/(qx), 1≤q≤Q and gcd(a,q)=1. The bound is uniform even when x−m is bounded.
     1	# Proof of P3
     2	
     3	We prove the stronger estimate
     4	\[
     5	\left|C_x(m)-(x-m)\mathfrak S(m)\right|
     6	\le B_\varepsilon x^{2/3+\varepsilon}
     7	\qquad (x\ge2,\ 1\le m\le x),
     8	\tag{1}
     9	\]
    10	where \(m\) is an integer and \(B_\varepsilon\) depends only on
    11	\(\varepsilon>0\). No published result is needed; in particular, no
    12	circle-method estimate is assumed.
    13	
    14	Put \(X=x-m\) and \(H=\lfloor x^{1/3}\rfloor\). All sums over \(n\) below
    15	are over integers, even when their upper limits are real. Thus \(X\ge0\),
    16	\(H\ge1\), and
    17	\[
    18	\frac12x^{1/3}\le H\le x^{1/3}.
    19	\tag{2}
    20	\]
    21	Indeed, \(\lfloor t\rfloor\ge t/2\) for every real \(t\ge1\).
    22	
    23	## 1. An elementary divisor bound
    24	
    25	For \(\delta>0\), define the finite constant
    26	\[
    27	K_\delta=\prod_{p<2^{1/\delta}}(1-p^{-\delta})^{-2},
    28	\tag{3}
    29	\]
    30	where an empty product is \(1\). We will use
    31	\[
    32	\tau(k)\le K_\delta k^\delta\qquad(k\ge1).
    33	\tag{4}
    34	\]
    35	To prove it, write \(k=\prod_p p^{a_p}\). If
    36	\(p\ge2^{1/\delta}\), the inequality \(a+1\le2^a\), valid for every
    37	integer \(a\ge0\), gives
    38	\((a+1)p^{-\delta a}\le1\). If \(p<2^{1/\delta}\), then
    39	\[
    40	(a+1)p^{-\delta a}
    41	\le\sum_{j=0}^\infty(j+1)p^{-\delta j}
    42	=(1-p^{-\delta})^{-2}.
    43	\]
    44	Multiplication over the prime factors of \(k\) proves (4).
    45	
    46	## 2. Truncating the two square-divisor sums
    47	
    48	For a positive integer \(k\), let
    49	\[
    50	A_H(k)=\sum_{\substack{d\le H\\d^2\mid k}}\mu(d),
    51	\qquad
    52	R_H(k)=\sum_{\substack{d>H\\d^2\mid k}}1.
    53	\]
    54	The exact identity
    55	\[
    56	\mu^2(k)=\sum_{d^2\mid k}\mu(d)
    57	\tag{5}
    58	\]
    59	follows by factoring the sum into \(\prod_{p^2\mid k}(1-1)\): it is
    60	\(1\) when no prime square divides \(k\), and \(0\) otherwise. Consequently,
    61	\[
    62	|\mu^2(k)-A_H(k)|\le R_H(k),\qquad
    63	|A_H(k)|\le\tau(k).
    64	\tag{6}
    65	\]
    66	
    67	We first bound the total discarded count. The outer sum in
    68	\(\sum_{k\le x}R_H(k)\) has \(\lfloor x\rfloor\) terms. Reversing the
    69	finite sums gives
    70	\[
    71	\sum_{k\le x}R_H(k)
    72	=\sum_{H<d\le\sqrt{x}}\left\lfloor\frac{x}{d^2}\right\rfloor
    73	\le x\sum_{d>H}\frac1{d^2}
    74	\le\frac{x}{H}.
    75	\tag{7}
    76	\]
    77	Here there are \(\max(0,\lfloor\sqrt{x}\rfloor-H)\) terms before
    78	extending the \(d\)-sum; each is at most \(x/d^2\). The last inequality
    79	uses \(\sum_{d>H}d^{-2}\le\int_H^\infty t^{-2}\,dt=H^{-1}\).
    80	
    81	For \(1\le n\le X\), both \(n\) and \(n+m\) belong to
    82	\([1,x]\). The exact decomposition
    83	\[
    84	\begin{split}
    85	\mu^2(n)\mu^2(n+m)-A_H(n)A_H(n+m)
    86	={}&(\mu^2(n)-A_H(n))\mu^2(n+m)\\
    87	&+A_H(n)(\mu^2(n+m)-A_H(n+m))
    88	\end{split}
    89	\]
    90	and (4), (6) imply the pointwise bound
    91	\[
    92	\left|\mu^2(n)\mu^2(n+m)-A_H(n)A_H(n+m)\right|
    93	\le R_H(n)+K_\delta x^\delta R_H(n+m).
    94	\]
    95	There are \(\lfloor X\rfloor\) terms in the \(n\)-sum. Each of the maps
    96	\(n\mapsto n\) and \(n\mapsto n+m\) is injective into the positive
    97	integers at most \(x\). Therefore (7) bounds each of the two sums of
    98	\(R_H\) by \(x/H\), and
    99	\[
   100	C_x(m)=\sum_{n\le X}A_H(n)A_H(n+m)+E_1,
   101	\qquad
   102	|E_1|\le(1+K_\delta x^\delta)\frac{x}{H}.
   103	\tag{8}
   104	\]
   105	This remains valid for \(0\le X<1\), when both \(n\)-sums are empty.
   106	
   107	## 3. Counting the truncated congruences
   108	
   109	For \(1\le d,e\le H\), put \(g=\gcd(d,e)\). The congruences
   110	\[
   111	n\equiv0\pmod{d^2},\qquad n\equiv-m\pmod{e^2}
   112	\tag{9}
   113	\]
   114	are compatible if and only if \(g^2\mid m\). For completeness, necessity
   115	follows by subtracting the congruences. For sufficiency, write
   116	\(d=ga\), \(e=gb\), with \(\gcd(a,b)=1\). Substitution of \(n=d^2t\)
   117	reduces (9) to
   118	\[
   119	a^2t\equiv-m/g^2\pmod{b^2},
   120	\]
   121	which has exactly one residue class of solutions for \(t\) modulo
   122	\(b^2\), because \(a^2\) is invertible modulo \(b^2\). Hence (9)
   123	defines one residue class modulo
   124	\[
   125	L=d^2b^2=\frac{d^2e^2}{g^2}.
   126	\]
   127	The count of positive integers in one residue class modulo \(L\) up to
   128	any real \(X\ge0\) differs from \(X/L\) by at most \(1\). Explicitly,
   129	choose its representative \(r\) with \(1\le r\le L\). The count is
   130	\(\lfloor(X+L-r)/L\rfloor\), and subtracting \(X/L\) gives a number
   131	between \(-1\) and \(1\).
   132	
   133	Define
   134	\[
   135	S_H(m)=\sum_{\substack{d,e\le H\\\gcd(d,e)^2\mid m}}
   136	\frac{\mu(d)\mu(e)\gcd(d,e)^2}{d^2e^2}.
   137	\]
   138	Expanding the finite product of divisor sums and applying the preceding
   139	count gives
   140	\[
   141	\sum_{n\le X}A_H(n)A_H(n+m)=X S_H(m)+E_2,
   142	\qquad |E_2|\le H^2.
   143	\tag{10}
   144	\]
   145	Indeed, there are \(H^2\) ordered pairs \((d,e)\). An incompatible pair
   146	contributes no error; a compatible pair has counting error at most \(1\),
   147	and its coefficient \(\mu(d)\mu(e)\) has absolute value at most \(1\).
   148	Thus summing these errors gives precisely the stated bound \(H^2\).
   149	
   150	## 4. The infinite coefficient and its uniform tail
   151	
   152	Set
   153	\[
   154	S_\infty(m)=\sum_{\substack{d,e\ge1\\\gcd(d,e)^2\mid m}}
   155	\frac{\mu(d)\mu(e)\gcd(d,e)^2}{d^2e^2}.
   156	\]
   157	This series is absolutely convergent. To verify that assertion, write
   158	\(d=ga\), \(e=gb\), where \(g=\gcd(d,e)\), and remove both the
   159	restriction \(g^2\mid m\) and the restriction \(\gcd(a,b)=1\) in an
   160	upper bound. Then
   161	\[
   162	\sum_{\substack{d,e\ge1\\\gcd(d,e)^2\mid m}}
   163	\frac{|\mu(d)\mu(e)|\gcd(d,e)^2}{d^2e^2}
   164	\le\sum_{g,a,b\ge1}\frac1{g^2a^2b^2}
   165	\le 8,
   166	\tag{11}
   167	\]
   168	since \(\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-2}\le1+\int_1^\infty t^{-2}\,dt=2\).
   169	
   170	For a finite set of primes, expand the sum restricted to squarefree
   171	\(d,e\) supported on that set. At a prime \(p\), the choices
   172	\((v_p(d),v_p(e))=(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\) contribute respectively
   173	\(1,-p^{-2},-p^{-2}\). The choice \((1,1)\) is allowed exactly when
   174	\(p^2\mid m\), and then contributes \(+p^{-2}\). Thus its local factor
   175	is
   176	\[
   177	1-\frac2{p^2}+\frac{\mathbf 1_{p^2\mid m}}{p^2}.
   178	\]
   179	By the absolute convergence in (11), passing through increasing finite
   180	sets of primes yields
   181	\[
   182	\begin{split}
   183	S_\infty(m)
   184	&=\prod_p\left(1-\frac2{p^2}
   185	                 +\frac{\mathbf 1_{p^2\mid m}}{p^2}\right)\\
   186	&=\prod_p\left(1-\frac2{p^2}\right)
   187	  \prod_{p^2\mid m}\frac{p^2-1}{p^2-2}
   188	=\mathfrak S(m).
   189	\end{split}
   190	\tag{12}
   191	\]
   192	The second product is finite because \(m\ge1\). The first product
   193	converges to a positive number: its factors are positive, and
   194	\(|\log(1-2/p^2)|\le4/p^2\), as follows by integrating
   195	\((1-u)^{-1}\le2\) for \(0\le u\le1/2\).
   196	
   197	Here is a tail estimate independent of \(m\). Define
   198	\[
   199	T_H=\sum_{\substack{d>H\\e\ge1}}
   200	\frac{\gcd(d,e)^2}{d^2e^2}.
   201	\]
   202	For every real \(t\ge1\),
   203	\[
   204	\sum_{a>t}a^{-2}\le\frac1{\lfloor t\rfloor}\le\frac2t;
   205	\]
   206	for \(0\le t<1\), the sum is at most \(2\). The decomposition
   207	\(d=ga\), \(e=gb\), with the coprimality condition removed in an
   208	upper bound, therefore gives
   209	\[
   210	\begin{split}
   211	T_H
   212	&\le\sum_{g\ge1}\frac1{g^2}
   213	       \left(\sum_{a>H/g}\frac1{a^2}\right)
   214	       \left(\sum_{b\ge1}\frac1{b^2}\right)\\
   215	&\le\frac4H\sum_{g=1}^H\frac1g
   216	       +4\sum_{g>H}\frac1{g^2}\\
   217	&\le\frac{4(1+\log H)}H+\frac4H
   218	 =\frac{4(2+\log H)}H.
   219	\end{split}
   220	\tag{13}
   221	\]
   222	In the first \(g\)-range there are exactly \(H\) terms, each bounded
   223	by \(4/(Hg)\); their sum is bounded by
   224	\(4(1+\log H)/H\). In the infinite second range, each term is at most
   225	\(4/g^2\); the integral tail bounds their sum by \(4/H\).
   226	
   227	The omitted pairs in \(S_H(m)\) have either \(d>H\) or \(e>H\).
   228	Removing the Möbius factors and compatibility restrictions bounds the
   229	first set by \(T_H\). Exchanging the names \(d,e\) in the second set
   230	bounds it by the same \(T_H\). The triangle inequality, (12), and (13)
   231	give
   232	\[
   233	|S_H(m)-\mathfrak S(m)|
   234	\le2T_H\le\frac{8(2+\log H)}H.
   235	\tag{14}
   236	\]
   237	In particular, define \(E_3=X(S_H(m)-\mathfrak S(m))\). Its bound after
   238	multiplication by \(X\) is
   239	\[
   240	|E_3|=|X(S_H(m)-\mathfrak S(m))|
   241	\le\frac{8x(2+\log H)}H,
   242	\tag{15}
   243	\]
   244	because \(0\le X\le x\).
   245	
   246	## 5. Combining the errors and checking the ranges
   247	
   248	Equations (8), (10), and (15) give the exact decomposition
   249	\[
   250	C_x(m)-X\mathfrak S(m)=E_1+E_2+E_3
   251	\]
   252	with the explicit bound
   253	\[
   254	\left|C_x(m)-X\mathfrak S(m)\right|
   255	\le H^2+\frac{x}{H}
   256	       \left(1+K_\delta x^\delta+8(2+\log H)\right).
   257	\tag{16}
   258	\]
   259	Using (2) and \(\log H\le\tfrac13\log x\), we obtain
   260	\[
   261	\begin{split}
   262	\left|C_x(m)-X\mathfrak S(m)\right|
   263	&\le x^{2/3}
   264	       \left(35+2K_\delta x^\delta+\frac{16}{3}\log x\right)\\
   265	&\le\left(35+2K_\delta+\frac{16}{3\delta}\right)
   266	       x^{2/3+\delta}.
   267	\end{split}
   268	\tag{17}
   269	\]
   270	For the last step, \(x^\delta\ge1\) and
   271	\[
   272	\log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}
   273	\le\int_1^x t^{\delta-1}\,dt
   274	=\frac{x^\delta-1}{\delta}\le\frac{x^\delta}{\delta}.
   275	\]
   276	Take \(\delta=\varepsilon\). Since
   277	\(2/3+\varepsilon\le4/5+\varepsilon\) and \(x\ge2\), the proposition
   278	holds with, for example,
   279	\[
   280	C(\varepsilon)=35+2K_\varepsilon+\frac{16}{3\varepsilon}.
   281	\]
   282	This proves (1) and the requested estimate. All preceding bounds are
   283	independent of \(m\) in its specified range and require no lower bound
   284	on \(X=x-m\). They therefore include bounded \(X\), including \(X=0\).
   285	
   286	The stated optional circle-method cutoff is also consistent with its
   287	specified range: for \(Q=x^{2/5}\),
   288	\[
   289	Q\le\frac{x^{1/2}}2
   290	\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^{1/10}\ge2
   291	\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\ge1024.
   292	\]
   293	For these \(x\), its arcs are well-defined subsets of \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\).
   294	They are disjoint: distinct reduced centers of denominators \(q,r\le Q\)
   295	have circular distance at least \(1/(qr)\), whereas the sum of their
   296	radii is
   297	\[
   298	\frac{Q}{qx}+\frac{Q}{rx}
   299	=\frac{Q(q+r)}{qr x}
   300	\le\frac{2Q^2}{qr x}
   301	\le\frac1{2qr}<\frac1{qr}.
   302	\]
   303	The proof above does not require this cutoff or any restriction to large
   304	\(x\).
   305	
   306	## Numerical sanity checks and sources
   307	
   308	As a check only, a Python calculation tested the truncated congruence
   309	count and its total error bound \(H^2\) for all permitted integer shifts
   310	at \(x=2,3,10,31,100,10.75,31.2\), comprising \(187\) pairs \((x,m)\).
   311	Using exact rational arithmetic, it also checked the finite Euler-product
   312	expansion in (12), restricted to the primes \(2,3,5,7\), for
   313	\(1\le m\le100\). The proof does not rely on these computations.
   314	
   315	No external source was used, and no excluded source was consulted.

1	# P1: Local densities and summable spectral coefficients
     2	
     3	Let μ be the Möbius function, φ Euler's totient, ζ the Riemann zeta function, and c=ζ(2)^(−1). All products below are over primes. For every integer q≥1 and integer l, the density g(q,l) from problem.md equals q^(−1)Σ_{m≥1, gcd(m²,q)|l} μ(m)gcd(m²,q)/m². Equivalently, it is zero if some p² divides both q and l; otherwise it equals (c/q)∏_{p|q}(1−p^(−2))^(−1)∏_{p||q, p|l}(1−p^(−1)). In particular 0≤g(q,l)≤1/q. Define the multiplicative function G by G(1)=1, G(p)=G(p²)=−1/(p²−1), and G(p^a)=0 for a≥3. Put γ(r)=cG(r), λ(r)=φ(r)γ(r)², and c_r(n)=Σ_{1≤a≤r, gcd(a,r)=1} exp(2πian/r). Then qΣ_{l=1}^q g(q,l)²=Σ_{r|q}λ(r), Σ_{r≥1}λ(r)=c, and, for every integer n≥1, the absolutely convergent series Σ_{r≥1}γ(r)²c_r(n) equals 𝔖(n)=∏_p(1−2/p²)∏_{p²|n}(p²−1)/(p²−2). There is an absolute constant C such that, uniformly for real R≥2, Σ_{r>R}λ(r)≤CR^(−1/2)(log(2R))² and Σ_{r≤R}rλ(r)≤CR^(1/2)(log(2R))².

item.text: The truncation and congruence counts check out, including when \(x-m<1\). The coefficient tail is bounded independently of \(m\) by \(O((1+\log H)/H)\). I’m checking the final constants and exponents; the proof uses no cited results or dependencies.

/bin/zsh -c "python3 -c 'import math
from fractions import Fraction
from sympy import mobius
cases = [(x,m) for x in (2,3,10,31,100,10.75,31.2,127.999,512.25) for m in range(1,math.floor(x)+1)]
mu = [0]+[int(mobius(d)) for d in range(1,math.isqrt(513)+1)]
for x,m in cases:
    H = max(h for h in range(1,10) if h**3 <= x)
    X=x-m
    N=math.floor(X)
    A=lambda k: sum(mu[d] for d in range(1,H+1) if k%(d*d)==0)
    truncated=sum(A(n)*A(n+m) for n in range(1,N+1))
    SH=Fraction(0)
    for d in range(1,H+1):
        for e in range(1,H+1):
            g=math.gcd(d,e)
            if m%(g*g)==0:
                L=d*d*e*e//(g*g)
                count=sum(n%(d*d)==0 and (n+m)%(e*e)==0 for n in range(1,N+1))
                assert abs(Fraction(count)-Fraction(X)/L)<=1
                SH+=Fraction(mu[d]*mu[e],L)
    assert abs(Fraction(truncated)-Fraction(X)*SH)<=H*H
    R=lambda k: sum(k%(d*d)==0 for d in range(H+1,math.isqrt(k)+1))
    assert sum(R(k) for k in range(1,math.floor(x)+1))<=Fraction(x)/H
print(f\"Checked congruence counts, the H"'^2 total error, and discarded-count bounds for {len(cases)} cases, including real x and endpoint shifts.")'"'"
